patch.value: Command-grammar conformance gate: the noun-verb table and shared verb vocabulary become machine-checked contracts a non-conforming command cannot pass

The consolidation epic can collapse 75 spellings into twelve nouns, but nothing prevents the surface from regrowing the day after: every prior census (60, 64, 65, 73, 75 commands) found new top-level spellings that had leaked in between passes. Consolidation without a gate is a one-time cleanup, not a property. This task makes the target grammar an executable contract: an allowlist of top-level nouns, a shared verb vocabulary with one meaning per verb, and the scope-before-verb ordering rule, all declared in the contracts table and enforced by a CI check that fails on any command, subcommand, or alias that does not conform. Hidden aliases are explicitly exempt and must be declared as aliases rather than as commands, which also gives pm-0mox a place to hang usage counters.

The contracts table declares the permitted top-level nouns, the shared verb vocabulary with one documented meaning per verb, and the scope-before-verb ordering rule as data, not prose; A CI check fails when a command, subcommand, or newly registered extension surface introduces a top-level noun outside the allowlist, a verb outside the vocabulary, or a scope-after-verb ordering; Hidden deprecated spellings must be declared as aliases of a conforming target and are exempt from the noun allowlist while still being counted; The gate reports the offending spelling and the nearest conforming target so the failure is self-correcting; The gate runs on the same job as the contracts drift check and cannot be satisfied by regenerating artifacts alone
The simplified surface is a maintained invariant rather than a completed migration
Every census since 2026-07-05 found the surface had grown between passes. A consolidation that is not gated will be re-litigated by the next feature that wants a top-level verb.
Turns the one-screen surface into a property enforced by CI, so agent-legibility survives contributors, extensions, and time without another manual census.
A declared noun and verb contract plus a failing CI check that makes non-conforming surface additions impossible to merge.
The twelve-noun target table now exists on this epic; gating it before the migrations start means each migration lands into an enforced shape instead of a convention.

value.text: Surface-growth measurement for the conformance gate this item defines (2026-07-25): pm --help now lists 78 top-level commands in this repo (76 in the isolated fixture the token-budget gate measures) across 109 lines. pm-n7rr's charter was written against roughly 60 and targets roughly 15 nouns, so the surface has grown by about a third while the consolidation epic has been open. The 78 include all eight list-* status variants, four history-* commands, three completion-* data providers, three lifecycle aliases (start-task, pause-task, close-task), three calendar shortcuts (meet, event, remind), and package-registered commands (beads, changelog, dedupe-audit, dedupe-merge, comments-audit, normalize, item, pm). This is the concrete baseline the grammar gate has to freeze: without it the count has no ceiling, and every new command adds to the 49,872-token full help surface agents pay to discover the tool.

value.text: Prerequisite discovered 2026-07-26: the twelve-noun target table on pm-n7rr has no placement for five live CORE nouns — graph, merge, events, copy, normalize — three of which (graph, merge, events) shipped after the table was authored. A conformance gate built against the current table would reject shipped functionality. Sequence the placement decision (recorded on pm-n7rr, ruled by ADR pm-pbyu) before the allowlist is declared as data, otherwise the allowlist encodes the omission.
